# Architecture catalog

Evidence catalog date: 2026-09-29. For changing B2 product details, use <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning> as the authority.

## CVAT annotation pipeline on Backblaze B2

Collect images, annotate in CVAT, validate COCO exports, publish immutable dataset versions, and deliver them directly from B2.

**Use when:** Keep large source media and customer-ready dataset releases durable and independently scalable while CVAT retains transactional annotation state on block storage.

**Workflow:** Collect raw media into a source bucket → Attach B2 to CVAT through its Amazon S3 provider and custom endpoint → Export annotations into a work bucket → Validate schema, label bounds, coverage, and checksums → Publish an immutable version and write its release manifest last → Deliver with short-lived presigned URLs and trigger downstream refresh

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Scoped application keys, Multipart upload, Presigned URLs and CORS, Event notifications, Object versions and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2 and Object Lock, Cloud Replication for disaster recovery.

**Integrations:** [CVAT](https://docs.cvat.ai/docs/workspace/attach-cloud-storage/) — Amazon S3 cloud storage with a Backblaze B2 endpoint URL.

**Scale:** Large image and video collections with many sequential object reads and writes. Standard B2 is the default; measure sustained multi-GPU or parallel refresh throughput before considering Overdrive or a compute-local cache.

**Security:** Use separate prefix-scoped keys for ingest, annotation reads, exports, publishing, and delivery signing; Treat presigned URLs and delivery manifests as bearer credentials; Keep administrative keys out of runtime services; Use governance-mode Object Lock by default and choose compliance mode only for a contractual requirement.

**Evidence basis:** CVAT documentation and source review; B2 documentation and CLI shape review; Moto-backed S3 application tests.

## Label Studio annotation pipeline on Backblaze B2

Sync source objects into Label Studio, write completed annotations to target storage, validate them, and publish customer-ready dataset versions on B2.

**Use when:** Give Label Studio controlled access to large image, audio, video, text, or task files without using object storage for its transactional application state.

**Workflow:** Upload source media or task definitions into a raw-data prefix → Connect a Label Studio S3 source storage using the B2 endpoint → Serve media through presigned URLs or the Label Studio storage proxy → Connect a separate S3 target storage for completed annotations → Validate exported tasks and media references → Publish immutable releases with the shared release contract → Deliver customer-specific, short-lived download URLs

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with a custom endpoint, Prefix-scoped application keys, Presigned URLs or application-proxied media, CORS for direct browser reads, Object versions and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2 and Object Lock, Event notifications for downstream validation.

**Integrations:** [Label Studio](https://labelstud.io/guide/storage_s3) — Amazon S3 source and target storage with the Backblaze B2 S3 endpoint.

**Scale:** Multimodal annotation projects whose source media is larger than the Label Studio application filesystem. Presigned delivery keeps media traffic off Label Studio workers; proxy mode trades simpler browser access for higher application bandwidth and worker load.

**Security:** Use separate source-reader and target-writer keys with the narrowest bucket prefix; Do not enable target deletion unless the workflow requires it; Restrict who can configure custom storage endpoints in Label Studio; Treat presigned URLs as temporary bearer credentials and configure CORS to the Label Studio origin.

**Evidence basis:** Label Studio source and target storage documentation review; Label Studio boto3 custom-endpoint source review; B2 S3 compatibility and key capability review.

## Dataloop DDOE direct-data pipeline on Backblaze B2

Connect Dataloop DDOE to B2 through its generic S3 API integration, process datasets without making the platform the system of record, and publish governed releases back to B2.

**Use when:** Run dataset synchronization, preprocessing, annotation, and AI applications against durable object storage while keeping B2 as the authoritative data and release layer.

**Workflow:** Ingest source objects and a stable inventory into a B2 raw-data prefix → Configure a DDOE S3 API integration with the regional B2 endpoint → Attach the storage integration to a compute cluster and synchronize a dataset → Run preprocessing, annotation, enrichment, or AI applications in DDOE → Export approved outputs and quality reports into a B2 work prefix → Validate and publish an immutable release with its manifest written last → Deliver the release through short-lived presigned URLs

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API with a configurable endpoint URL, Direct data access without mandatory source-object duplication, Prefix-scoped application keys, Object versions and lifecycle rules, Event notifications for validation and downstream refresh, SSE-B2 and Object Lock for governed releases, Presigned customer delivery.

**Integrations:** [Dataloop DDOE](https://docs.dataloop.ai/docs/s3-api) — Generic S3 API storage integration configured with the regional Backblaze B2 endpoint; B2-specific acceptance testing is required.

**Scale:** Enterprise image, video, document, LiDAR, and multimodal collections processed by Kubernetes-hosted applications and pipelines. Keep source objects in B2 and measure synchronization, preview generation, and parallel read patterns with representative object sizes before production rollout.

**Security:** Scope the DDOE source key to only the bucket and prefix synchronized into the platform; Put generated previews, platform metadata, and processing outputs in an explicitly writable prefix rather than granting broad raw-data writes; Keep release publication and Object Lock credentials outside DDOE runtime applications; Restrict who can create storage integrations because endpoint and credential configuration controls server-side data access.

**Evidence basis:** Dataloop DDOE generic S3 API documentation review; Dataloop storage integration and dataset synchronization documentation review; B2 S3 endpoint and application-key capability mapping.

## Supervisely annotation and dataset pipeline on Backblaze B2

Connect Supervisely to B2 through its configurable S3-compatible storage paths, annotate or transform remote media, and publish immutable dataset releases.

**Use when:** Work with large image and video collections in Supervisely while keeping durable source media, exports, and customer releases in independently governed object storage.

**Workflow:** Collect source images and video into a B2 raw-data prefix → Configure Supervisely remote storage or a team cloud connection with the regional B2 endpoint → Import existing media by reference when the selected Supervisely workflow supports remote links → Annotate, review, transform, or run Supervisely applications → Export approved datasets and reports into a B2 work prefix → Validate and publish an immutable release with its manifest written last → Deliver the release with customer-specific presigned URLs

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible storage with a configurable endpoint, Remote media links and cloud import/export workflows, Multipart upload for large artifacts, Prefix-scoped application keys, Object versions and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2 and Object Lock, Presigned delivery and downstream events.

**Integrations:** [Supervisely](https://docs.supervisely.com/enterprise-edition/advanced-tuning/s3) — S3-compatible remote storage or team cloud storage configured with the regional Backblaze B2 endpoint.

**Scale:** Large image and video projects with interactive annotation, model-assisted processing, and repeated dataset export. Direct links avoid unnecessary source copies, while preview caches and interactive reads still require capacity and latency testing near Supervisely compute.

**Security:** Use different credentials for linked source reads and export writes; Restrict remote-storage administration and never expose application keys in project assets or link files; Keep release signing and retention credentials outside Supervisely; Treat exported presigned URLs and delivery manifests as bearer credentials.

**Evidence basis:** Supervisely S3-compatible remote-storage documentation review; Supervisely cloud import, remote-link, and export documentation review; B2 S3 endpoint, multipart, and application-key capability mapping.

## FiftyOne dataset curation and quality pipeline on Backblaze B2

Reference B2-backed media from FiftyOne Enterprise, curate and evaluate datasets on compute, and publish selected samples, labels, and quality evidence as immutable releases.

**Use when:** Inspect, search, deduplicate, evaluate, and select large datasets without turning the curation platform database into the durable release system of record.

**Workflow:** Store source media and a stable inventory in a B2 raw-data prefix → Configure a custom-endpoint cloud credential path in FiftyOne Enterprise and test it against B2 → Create a FiftyOne dataset whose sample filepaths resolve to B2-backed media → Compute embeddings, similarity, quality, duplicate, and evaluation views on external compute → Export selected samples, labels, reports, and provenance into a B2 work prefix → Validate and publish an immutable curated release with its manifest written last → Deliver releases through presigned URLs or downstream compute access

**B2 capabilities:** Cloud-backed media references, Custom endpoint configuration through the MinIO-compatible credential path, Managed bucket-scoped cloud credentials, Prefix-scoped B2 application keys, Immutable versioned release objects, SSE-B2, Object Lock, and lifecycle policies, Presigned delivery and compute-local caching.

**Integrations:** [FiftyOne Enterprise](https://docs.voxel51.com/enterprise/installation.html) — Candidate custom-endpoint connection through FiftyOne's documented MinIO-compatible cloud-media configuration; validate B2 addressing and media access before adoption.

**Scale:** Large computer-vision and multimodal datasets requiring interactive exploration, embeddings, quality analysis, and curated subset releases. Media remains object-backed, but databases, indexes, embeddings, previews, and frequently reused objects may need storage or caching close to FiftyOne compute.

**Security:** Use read-only credentials for raw media and separate writers for reports or selected outputs; Scope managed cloud credentials to the smallest possible bucket set and user or group audience; Keep FiftyOne's database, indexes, session state, and secrets off B2 dataset prefixes; Do not store expiring presigned URLs as durable sample identifiers.

**Evidence basis:** FiftyOne Enterprise cloud-backed media documentation review; FiftyOne MinIO-compatible endpoint and managed-credential documentation review; B2 S3 addressing, credential, and object-access requirements analysis.

## Roboflow presigned import and release pipeline with Backblaze B2

Select B2 objects, give Roboflow time-limited read URLs for API import, process the copied assets in Roboflow, and return approved exports to governed B2 releases.

**Use when:** Move selected computer-vision assets through a managed processing platform without public buckets, permanent shared credentials, or an unsupported direct-B2 connector claim.

**Workflow:** Store private source images and metadata in a B2 raw-data prefix → Select an import batch from a stable inventory or manifest → Generate short-lived B2 presigned GET URLs with a read-only key → Submit each URL to the Roboflow upload API and record the returned asset identity → Annotate, preprocess, augment, version, or train inside Roboflow → Export approved data and model-independent dataset artifacts back to a B2 work prefix → Validate and publish an immutable release with its manifest written last

**B2 capabilities:** Short-lived presigned GET URLs, API-mediated import without public B2 buckets, Prefix-scoped source-reader and output-writer keys, Deterministic import inventories and provenance mapping, Object versions and lifecycle policies, SSE-B2 and Object Lock for final releases, Customer delivery from B2.

**Integrations:** [Roboflow](https://docs.roboflow.com/datasets/create-and-upload/adding-data/upload-data-from-aws-gcp-and-azure/aws-s3-bucket) — One-time or scripted import through B2 presigned URLs submitted to the Roboflow API; this architecture does not claim B2 support in Roboflow Bucket Mirror.

**Scale:** Selected computer-vision batches imported into a managed platform for labeling, transformation, dataset versioning, or training. Presigned import is best for bounded or scripted transfers; large continuous synchronization should be evaluated separately because Roboflow's documented persistent datasource path is AWS-specific.

**Security:** Generate URLs from a read-only key scoped to the selected source prefix and keep expiry only as long as the import queue requires; Treat Roboflow as a separate data processor because imported objects are copied across the trust boundary; Store the Roboflow API credential in a secret manager and never embed it in URLs, manifests, or B2 object metadata; Use separate credentials and validation for exports returning to B2.

**Evidence basis:** Roboflow AWS S3 and presigned-URL import documentation review; Roboflow upload API flow review; Repository-tested B2-compatible presigned URL generation pattern review.
